skill.name: linux-production-shell-scripts
skill.description: Generate and adapt Linux shell script templates for backups, monitoring, user management, log review, network checks, and routine automation.
skill.summary: Create practical Linux administration shell scripts from reusable production-style templates.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation with Bash templates, so many Markdown backtick and shebang findings are false positives. Real risks remain in privileged package and service commands, cron and nohup persistence patterns, account inventory, destructive file operations, remote SSH execution, and unsafe secret handling examples.

remediation.issue: Privileged commands and service control appear in runnable templates.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation prompts, dry-run modes, allowlists, and rollback guidance before any sudo, package, or systemctl action.

remediation.issue: Cron, nohup, and remote SSH execution examples can create persistence or remote impact.
remediation.suggestion: Require operators to provide explicit schedules and hosts, document removal steps, and include audit logging for scheduled or remote execution.

remediation.issue: Deletion templates can remove unintended data.
remediation.suggestion: Add path validation, dry-run output, protected directory checks, and backups before using rm, find -exec rm, or rsync --delete.

remediation.issue: Secret examples use inline passwords and print generated passwords.
remediation.suggestion: Use protected prompts, environment variables, or a secret manager, and avoid echoing sensitive values into logs or terminal history.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Script Execution Template
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes an SSH template that sends a local script to a remote server and runs it with bash. This can execute unreviewed local content on another host if users accept defaults or provide the wrong target.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SSH command explicitly runs a supplied script on a remote server. This is a direct remote execution pattern with clear administrative impact.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive File Operation Templates
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes rsync deletion and find-based removal templates. These patterns can delete large amounts of data when paths, variables, or retention values are wrong.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands include rsync --delete and rm execution through find. Both are valid admin tools, but the destructive behavior is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Secret Handling Examples
semantic_findings.description: The database backup template uses a password variable in the script, and the password generator prints generated passwords to standard output. These examples can encourage secret exposure in logs, shells, or files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples visibly place a database password in a shell variable and echo generated passwords. The issue is contextual and not covered by the static patterns.

dangerous_patterns.title: System reconnaissance
dangerous_patterns.confidence_reasoning: The system info collector names its report with the hostname and gathers host details. This is expected admin inventory but still system reconnaissance.

dangerous_patterns.title: System reconnaissance

content.value_statement: Linux teams need repeatable scripts for common administration work. This skill provides structured Bash templates for backups, monitoring, logs, users, networking, and automation.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Bash templates for file backups, backup rotation, and database backups.
Creates monitoring scripts for CPU, disk, system health, and uptime checks.
Provides user management examples for account creation and password expiry reporting.
Builds log analysis, network diagnostics, and web server report scripts.
Supplies automation patterns for package installation, cron scheduling, services, cleanup, and Git updates.
Includes quick references for Bash syntax, common commands, and cron timing.
limitations: Templates require review before use on production systems.
Some examples need root privileges or system package managers.
Scripts assume common Linux utilities and may need distribution-specific changes.
The skill does not verify permissions, secrets handling, or rollback behavior automatically.

use_cases.title: Create Backup Jobs
use_cases.description: Generate scripts for local archives, remote rsync backups, database dumps, and simple backup rotation.

use_cases.title: Monitor Server Health
use_cases.description: Build scripts that record CPU, disk, uptime, process, memory, and service status for routine checks.

use_cases.title: Automate Maintenance Tasks
use_cases.description: Prepare repeatable scripts for cleanup, package installation, cron scheduling, and repository updates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Backup Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for local file protection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash script that backs up one directory to another directory with a timestamped archive. Include clear variables and basic error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Monitoring Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linux monitoring script that checks CPU and disk usage against thresholds and writes a timestamped alert log.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Maintenance Script
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for safer production use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this shell script for quoting, permissions, destructive commands, logging, and rollback concerns. Suggest safer changes before production use.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Automation Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for a managed server fleet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a set of Bash scripts for backups, log analysis, cleanup, and service checks. Include dry-run modes, configuration variables, and operational safeguards.

output_examples.input: Create a backup script for /srv/app that keeps seven archives.
output_examples.output: A Bash backup plan with configurable source and destination paths, timestamped archive names, retention logic, and notes for testing restore behavior.

output_examples.input: Check whether Apache is running and restart it when needed.
output_examples.output: A service maintenance script outline that checks service status, logs each action, uses privileged commands only when required, and reports failures clearly.

output_examples.input: Summarize errors from a Linux system log.
output_examples.output: A log analysis approach that selects a log file, filters important error terms, counts matches, and writes a dated report for review.

best_practices: Run generated scripts first in a non-production test environment.
Replace placeholders with explicit paths, users, hosts, and thresholds before execution.
Add dry-run, logging, confirmation, and backup steps around destructive operations.
anti_patterns: Running generated scripts as root without reading every command first.
Embedding real passwords, tokens, or private hostnames in script files.
Scheduling cron jobs or remote execution before validating paths and permissions.

faq.question: Can this skill run shell scripts for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides script templates and guidance. Users must review and run scripts in their own environment.

faq.question: Does it support production Linux servers?
faq.answer: Yes, but every script should be tested and adapted to the target distribution, permissions, and operational policy.

faq.question: Can it create monitoring scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for CPU usage, disk usage, uptime checks, system health, and basic service monitoring.

faq.question: Can it manage users and passwords?
faq.answer: It includes administrative examples, but user and password tasks require strict permission controls and local policy review.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets safely by default?
faq.answer: No. Users should move secrets to approved secret stores or protected environment variables before production use.

faq.question: What should I review before using a generated script?
faq.answer: Review sudo usage, delete operations, cron changes, remote hosts, file paths, logging, and rollback steps.
